title: Club 78 and Tony Bennett's break at the Shangrila (second version)
summary: The Winchell story and the Shangrila, where Tony Bennett got his break.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Don't judge books by covers. Club 78; where was that?
That was down on 78th and Broadway.

That's right where I used to live. The bandleader, Snub Mosley, asked the patrons to call their favorites; Rhapsody in Blue someone shouted. Mosley realized the customer sneering at his band so he turned around and had his small, but competent, alto play Rhapsody perfectly, note for note, from beginning to end. Very good; what year was this? When were you at Club 78?
I was at Club 78 in 1948.
Yeah, right after I left
Shangrila.
Back up now; where is the Shangrila?
The Shangrila was right over here in Long Island. That's where a big story comes from.
I also recorded a number for Walter Thornton--
Who was Walter Thornton?
He was one of the big three of the model agencies, Hanover, Powell and Walter Thornton.
I did this--I had him on my show the other day; Joe Franklin had him on also. Pin up Girl.

He brought Bob Hope out to the Shangrila one night to hear me. Bob wanted somebody (inaudible). It was on a Monday night and I was off and it was a trio in the front, and a guitar player. They sat there at the bar for a while and they listened to this guy, and do you know who was on guitar? I little guy by the name of Anthony
Benedetti.
Tony Bennett.
That's where Tony Bennett got his break. I was off that night. Bob took him in.
Was that 1947 or '48?
I think it was '48.
The Shangrila was where?
Just as you get off the Triboro Bridge in Astoria, you make a left. We used to call that Long Island City. Would this be of any--
